utterances.text: Well, Mr. Sutalo, the last words you said were not recorded in the transcript. You said that it wasn't correct, or that you didn't know it?

utterances.speaker: LUKA SUTALO
utterances.text: Well, yes, I don't know about that, but I do know what I was told by this one person because I asked, Well, how come all of you are so young? And he said, Well, they are all released from a juvenile facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Sutalo, since you mentioned that they actually bought honey from you, would that mean that they actually paid for the honey, Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: LUKA SUTALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they paid it quite honestly, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sutalo, I have no further questions for you, and I wish you a long and good life. I see that you look very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That is all that I have for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Has the cross-examination triggered any need for further questions to Mr. Sutalo?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, only one brief matter of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sutalo, Ms. Friedman has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sutalo, you were asked today in the cross-examination just now about two people who were with you in Serbia called Zvonko Tucak and Mata, any I think there may have been some confusion. You were asked whether these people called you out and took you to the military officer Kosutic. Did these men take you to the officer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA SUTALO
utterances.text: No. No. They didn't take me, but because there was this unfortunate thing with the army entering, then Zeljko Zubovic came, he worked at the Erdut farm, he came and said that there were many Croats in Dalj that had been killed. So then I said that my wife and I should flee across until things quietened down a little bit, so when we went across, I was caught by the army, Kosutic's soldiers, and they took me to him. This is where I met Tucak and Mata from Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And were Tucak and Mata also being held there and detained there in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: LUKA SUTALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Bench has no further questions. And may I take it that the re-examination has not triggered any further need for questions to the witness. Mr. Sutalo, this concludes your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming to the place of the video conference and for having answered the questions that were put to you. You are excused, and I wish you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm grateful to you as well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wish you a safe return home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we can conclude the videolink. Thank you for your assistance, Ms. Veretelnikova, at a distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have a few matters, not very much. One is I'd like to have special attention for page 18, line 10, where I got the impression the witness was talking about Mr. Hadzic, Goran Hadzic, whereas it appears as Adzic and since Mr. Adzic also was a prominent person in the former Yugoslavia, we should take care that this is not in any way misrecorded or misunderstood. Then finally, Mr. Stanisic, you have asked whether you could address the Chamber for five minutes. Now, the Chamber is willing, although it's not very common, to give you an opportunity to address the Chamber. And from what I see, there's no need to give a solemn declaration because matters you will talk about are not related to matters we find in the indictment. However, although there would be time at this moment, one of the judges is not there. For that reason, it might be wiser to wait until Monday, so that all three judges have heard what you want to tell us. I see you are nodding yes, which I take it for agreeing to postponing it until next week. Is there any other procedural matter which requires our attention at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see no positive responses, and I hear no positive responses from the Defence, therefore, the Chamber takes it that the same is true for the Defence. Then under these circumstances, we'll adjourn, and we'll resume on Monday, the 8th of March, at quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 8th day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.16 p.m.
